What a VPN does—and doesn’t do

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerWhere the tunnel endsWho you are trustingWhen troubleshootingFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

A VPN creates an encrypted connection between your device and a VPN endpoint. It changes who handles part of your network traffic; it does not make you anonymous or protect you from every online threat.

Where the tunnel ends

A remote-access VPN can connect you to a workplace network. A consumer VPN typically routes internet traffic through a provider. Encryption supplied by the VPN covers the tunnel; HTTPS remains important for the connection to a website.

Who you are trusting

Your VPN provider takes a position of trust in the traffic path. Websites can still identify you through accounts, cookies, and other signals. A VPN does not stop a phishing page from asking for your password.

When troubleshooting

A VPN can affect access to local devices or some websites. If you control the VPN, disconnect briefly on a trusted network to isolate a connection issue. For a work-managed device, ask your IT team before changing required security settings.
